subject: EU processing: control-plane geofencing + SCCs integration plan
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Gunnar Svensson <gunnar@medsys-eu.com>, Elise Dubois <elise.dubois@medsys-legal.fr>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 May 2028 08:12:00 +0000
Subject: EU processing: control-plane geofencing + SCCs integration plan

Hi Gunnar / Elise —

Thanks again for the conversation earlier. As promised, attaching a lightweight diagram that shows our recommended approach to satisfy your EU-only processing requirement while remaining compatible with the SCCs-based transfer framework. High-level summary:

- Data plane (inference, user content, KV cache, and application logs) runs in our EU regions only.
- Control plane (orchestration + metadata) runs in our global control plane but we can configure it to avoid persisting user content.
- Operator/admin access can be restricted to EU operators for the MediSys tenant via our role bindings + dedicated audit trails.
- KMS keys for customer data can be provisioned in your AWS account (bring-your-own-key) in eu-west-1 — we will never hold plaintext.

Open questions we flagged for legal/ops: replication/backups of metrics & crash dumps (are those considered customer content for MediSys?), and whether you require a private (on-prem or VPC) deployment for full evidentiary separation.

Attachments: controlplane_geofence_draw_v1.pdf (diagram) — also uploaded to the shared Drive link below.

Next steps I propose: 1) confirm scope of "customer content" vs telemetry for MediSys; 2) pick one of the three technical options (quick pilot, dedicated VPC, or private deployment) so we can scope a DPA addendum; 3) schedule a short technical workshop.

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

From: Gunnar Svensson <gunnar@medsys-eu.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Elise Dubois <elise.dubois@medsys-legal.fr>
Date: Fri, 11 May 2028 09:35:00 +0200
Subject: Re: EU processing: control-plane geofencing + SCCs integration plan

Thanks Soojin — useful diagram. A few immediate items from our side:

- Operator access: we need clear contractual commitments that any operator access to customer data (including metadata that could re-identify) will be performed from within the EU/EEA. Is that enforceable operationally?
- Backups & DR: does your standard backup policy replicate snapshots out of region? We require all backups of MediSys customer content to remain in EU.
- Logs and crash dumps: we treat crash dumps as potential customer personal data — can those be redacted or retained only in EU?
- SCCs: our legal team will want to see the DPA + your SCCs annex and a short attestation that operator access procedures are in place.

I compiled our initial SCCs questions in the attached spreadsheet so you have line items to respond to.

Thanks — Gunnar
Gunnar Svensson
CISO, MediSys Health

Attachment: medsys_sccs_questions.xlsx

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 May 2028 10:00:00 +0000
Subject: RE: EU processing: control-plane geofencing + SCCs integration plan

Looping in some tech details to give a clearer set of options we can present back to MediSys (short bullets, pros/cons):

Option A — Private (on-prem or VPC private deployment):
- Pros: full in-region isolation, operator access fully under customer netops; easiest to satisfy strict legal asks.
- Cons: longer lead time, infra transfer/install, higher baseline cost.

Option B — Hosted + EU-only data plane + BYOK KMS in customer account (recommended pilot):
- Pros: fastest to stand up; data + KV cache + embeddings stored & processed in EU; KMS keys in MediSys AWS account eliminate server-side plaintext risk.
- Cons: control plane still in global region for orchestration; must provide operational attestation that control-plane metadata cannot be used to reconstruct customer data.

Option C — Hosted + SCCs + operator restrictions + cryptographic minimization:
- Pros: lower cost; supports standard hosted offering with contractual SCCs addendum and stricter operator guardrails.
- Cons: more legal negotiation for attestation and access controls; some customers view this as higher risk.

We should map Gunnar's spreadsheet to the options matrix and mark which items are "must have" vs "nice to have". I attached an options matrix doc (options_matrix.md) with the mapping and proposed timelines for a pilot (2-3 weeks) vs private deploy (8-12 weeks).

Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Principal Product Manager, Security & Privacy, Redwood Inference

From: Elise Dubois <elise.dubois@medsys-legal.fr>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Gunnar Svensson <gunnar@medsys-eu.com>
Date: Mon, 15 May 2028 14:20:00 +0200
Subject: Re: EU processing: control-plane geofencing + SCCs integration plan

Thank you for the options. A couple of legal points we need confirmed in writing before procurement can sign:

1) We require the ability to sign an amended SCCs annex and DPA that explicitly names operator access controls; please confirm you will accept this and provide a draft.
2) Retention policy for audit logs and backups: MediSys prefers maximum 5 years for backups and 2 years for detailed operator audit logs; please confirm your retention windows and deletion proof processes.
3) Evidence of deletion: we will need a deletion attestation workflow and a timeline for demonstration (test account) prior to go-live.
4) Schrems II acceptance: our counsel will want a short paragraph from Redwood on your risk mitigation measures (technical, contractual, organizational) regarding non-EU access under Schrems II.

Please let us have a DPA draft and suggested attestation language this week if possible so our procurement can progress.

Regards,
Elise
Elise Dubois
Head of Legal, MediSys Health

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Gunnar Svensson <gunnar@medsys-eu.com>, Elise Dubois <elise.dubois@medsys-legal.fr>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 May 2028 16:42:00 +0000
Subject: Re: EU processing: control-plane geofencing + SCCs integration plan

Hi Gunnar / Elise —

Thanks for the clear questions. Proposed path forward (summary):

- Pilot: we suggest moving forward with Option B (Hosted + EU-only data plane + BYOK in your AWS account) as a pilot. That gives MediSys in-region processing and rapid time-to-value.
- Retention: we can set default audit log retention to 24 months for detailed operator logs; backups retention can be scoped per-bucket and we can commit to keeping customer content backups in EU for MediSys (no cross-border replication).
- Operator access: we will bind "MediSys tenant" operator roles to our EU operations pool where feasible and provide time-limited access tokens. We will prepare an internal attestation statement about operator access locations and procedures.
- Evidence/deletion: Redwood will provide a deletion runbook and an evidence package (hash-based proof + screenshots + logs) for a test purge on a demo dataset.

Action items:
1) Naomi & Jonas to draft the DPA addendum + SCCs annex (Naomi: legal text; Jonas: technical attestation) — target 3 business days.
2) Aditya to provision a pilot EU-only tenant and BYOK integration instructions for MediSys (ETA 5 business days).
3) Soojin to schedule technical workshop and DocuSign DPA link (I have uploaded a draft DPA to Drive and included a DocuSign link below).

DocuSign (DPA draft): https://www.docusign.com/recipient?token=ABC123EXAMPLEDOCUSIGN
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-example-diagrams

If this approach is acceptable to MediSys we will start the pilot runbook and provide the attestation materials for review.

Best,
Soojin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
